items.passage: In any case it was dangerous, and an abomination that ought to have been done away with. Well, I was close to the edge of this hollow--there being a short cut to the Manchester road just beyond it--when Philip overtook me. He didn’t spare me, I can tell you, for, apart from the money question, there was an old sore between us. The girl he wanted to marry had done me the honour to prefer his father’s confidential clerk. She was a sensible girl, and saw the point to which our lives were drifting. When he had called me reptile, and a few other equally agreeable names, finding that he couldn’t sting me into retaliation by abuse of that kind, he came close up to me and struck me across the face with his open hand.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Philip in the text?
options: Coolly contemptuous of his insults and his temper
Deeply ashamed of having wronged him over money
Openly fearful that Philip will ruin his future
Warmly sympathetic toward his loss of the girl
items.explanation: 서술자는 Philip이 자신을 'reptile' 등으로 부른 것을 'equally agreeable names'라고 비꼬아 표현한다. 또 그 여자가 자신을 택한 일을 'done me the honour'라고 말하며 Philip의 분노에 전혀 동요하지 않는 태도를 보인다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 수치심, C의 두려움, D의 동정은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: I fancy I see it now, but I am not sure—not at all. Certainly the affair was too stupid—when I think of it—to be altogether natural. Still... But at the moment it presented itself simply as a confounded nuisance. The steamer was sunk. They had started two days before in a sudden hurry up the river with the manager on board, in charge of some volunteer skipper, and before they had been out three hours they tore the bottom out of her on stones, and she sank near the south bank. I asked myself what I was to do there, now my boat was lost.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the sinking of the steamer?
options: Grief for the crew who were lost in the river
Irritation mixed with suspicion about its cause
Relief that he had avoided a dangerous voyage
Admiration for the skipper's effort to save her
items.explanation: 서술자는 사건이 당시에는 'a confounded nuisance'로 느껴졌다고 말해 짜증을 드러낸다. 동시에 그 일이 'too stupid ... to be altogether natural'이라며 원인을 의심한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 선원의 죽음, 안도, 선장에 대한 감탄은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
"Meet me at breakfast alone,
And then I will give you a dish
Which really deserves to be known,
Though 'tis not the genteelest of fish.
You must promise to come, for I said
A splendid red herring I'd buy.
Nay, turn not aside your proud head;
You'll like it, I know, when you try.

"If moisture the herring betray,
Drain till from the moisture 'tis free.
Warm it through in the usual way,
Then serve it for you and for me.
A piece of cold butter prepare,
To rub it when ready it lies;
Egg sauce and potatoes don't spare,
And the flavour will cause you surprise."
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the red herring?
options: Embarrassed that the dish is unfit for a guest
Doubtful that the listener will ever accept it
Confidently enthusiastic despite its humble status
Indifferent to whether it is prepared correctly
items.explanation: 화자는 청어가 'not the genteelest of fish'라고 인정하면서도 'really deserves to be known'이라고 말한다. 또 'You'll like it, I know'와 'the flavour will cause you surprise'라며 확신에 찬 열의를 보인다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 부끄러움, B의 의심, D의 무관심은 화자의 자신감 있는 권유와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Were we framed merely that we might for a few years rejoice in the beauty of the stars, as in that of the flowers beneath our feet? And ought we to be grateful for those transitory glimpses of the heavens, as for the fading splendour of the earth? But the heavens are not an idle show, hung out for the gaze of that idle dreamer Man. They are the work of the Eternal God, and He has given us power therein to read and to understand His glory. It is not our eyes only that are dazzled by the face of heaven--our souls can comprehend the laws by which that face is overspread by its celestial smiles. The dwelling-place of our spirits is already in the heavens.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the heavens?
options: Mild amusement at people who study the stars
Regret that their beauty fades so quickly
Uncertainty about whether they can be understood
Reverent conviction that they reveal divine glory
items.explanation: 서술자는 하늘이 'not an idle show'이며 'the work of the Eternal God'이라고 단언한다. 또 인간의 영혼이 그 법칙을 이해할 수 있다고 말하며 경외와 확신을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 하늘이 덧없다는 생각(B)은 서술자가 반박하려고 던진 질문일 뿐이고, A와 C는 지문의 확신과 반대된다.

items.passage: Last night we heard the calls of natives at the opposite side of the river. As soon as they saw us, they crossed the river, and came pretty close to us: the discharge of our guns, however, kept them at a distance. Several of our party, during their watches saw them moving with fire sticks on the other side of the river. In the morning, three of them came boldly up; so I went to them with some presents, and they became very friendly indeed. Presents were exchanged; and they invited us in the most pressing manner to accompany them to their camp; and were evidently disappointed in finding that we could not swim.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the three visitors who came in the morning?
options: Friendly goodwill after an initially wary start
Lasting distrust despite the exchange of gifts
Amused scorn for their inability to cross water
Quiet indifference to their repeated invitations
items.explanation: 처음에 서술자 일행은 총을 쏘아 원주민들을 'at a distance'에 두며 경계했다. 그러나 아침에 서술자는 선물을 들고 그들에게 갔고 그들이 'very friendly indeed'가 되었다고 기록한다. 따라서 경계에서 호의로 바뀐 A가 정답이다. 헤엄치지 못한 것은 원주민이 아니라 서술자 일행이므로 C는 틀리고, B와 D도 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
I hasten to write, and beg you, as far as I am concerned, to pay no attention whatever to it. He was sent over to us by Lady Heton, a traveling acquaintance, whom we know really nothing of, and it's been a great bother trying to be civil and everything else to him. I felt obliged to give him the letter, but you will understand by this that you are to ignore it quite as much as you like. He is no friend of ours whatever, merely an acquaintance that has been forced upon us.

We hear you are having such a gay season in Washington. We think of taking a house there for next winter. Can you manage to keep out of the political set if you want to?
items.question: Which choice best describes the writer's attitude toward the man who carries the letter?
options: Gratitude for his help with Lady Heton
Dismissive annoyance at an unwanted acquaintance
Concern that he will suffer in Washington
Curiosity about his role in the political set
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 그 남자를 대하는 일이 'a great bother'였다고 말한다. 또 'no friend of ours whatever'라며 억지로 떠맡은 지인일 뿐이라고 강조하고 편지를 무시해도 된다고 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 감사(A), 걱정(C), 호기심(D)은 이 냉담한 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The King married her, uncanonically, it is true; but who was she to hold up church law before his face? Well, then she, by her own pure act, caused herself to be put away by the King, abjuring thus his kingly seat. Hey, but it is so, that by her own prayers, her proper pleading, her proper tears, she worked against her proper honour, and against the child in her womb. What more could she do? What more could any wife, any mother, than that? Ah, say that you hate her without stint, would you have her die?
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To condemn the King for ignoring church law
To describe the ceremony of a royal wedding
To argue that the queen's sacrifice deserves mercy
To explain why the queen hated her husband
items.explanation: 화자는 왕비가 'by her own pure act' 스스로 물러났고 자신의 명예와 아이까지 희생했다고 말한다. 이어 'What more could she do?'라고 묻고 'would you have her die?'라며 청자에게 자비를 호소한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 왕에 대한 비난(A), 결혼식 묘사(B), 왕비의 증오(D)는 지문의 중심이 아니다.

items.passage: My husband:—Once again I write to you from the depths of a weary heart, without hope, without a belief that you will ever see my letter, but I must speak to you before I die! for it seems to me impossible to live and face that woman. I wrote to you again and again, Louis. I told you of the terrible strait to which I was driven. I appealed to you from the depths of my humiliation. I besought you to give back my secret and send the proofs of our marriage before it was too late—before disgrace fell upon me, and the shelter of a respectable roof was taken from over my head.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To announce that the writer has forgiven Louis
To describe the woman the writer must now face
To recall the happy early days of a marriage
To make a desperate final plea to an absent husband
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 'without hope'라고 쓰면서도 'I must speak to you before I die!'라고 외친다. 또 반복해서 편지를 보내 결혼 증거를 돌려 달라고 'besought' 했다고 말한다. 따라서 절망 속의 마지막 호소인 D가 정답이다. 용서(A), 그 여자 묘사(B), 행복한 회상(C)은 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
A sob of agony told that her spirit was no more on earth. The soldiers, separating her gently from the body of the subah, upon whose knees her hands were clasped, bore her into the saloon, where they laid her upon a divan. They then conveyed the remains of the subah to his apartments in the castle, and watched by them during the remainder of the night.

The dawn of the following morning displayed a melancholy spectacle in those chambers, so lately the abode of mirth in its many forms. The prospect of a speedy peace had lent wings to every body engaged in those scenes of joy.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show a sudden shift from celebration to mourning
To explain how the soldiers won a speedy peace
To describe the design of the castle chambers
To criticize the soldiers for their harsh conduct
items.explanation: 지문은 여인이 숨을 거두고 병사들이 시신을 옮기는 장면을 그린다. 이어 아침의 'melancholy spectacle'이 'so lately the abode of mirth'였던 방들에 펼쳐졌다고 대비한다. 따라서 기쁨에서 슬픔으로의 급변을 보여 주는 A가 정답이다. 병사들은 'gently' 행동했으므로 D는 틀리고, B와 C는 지문의 초점이 아니다.

items.passage: Most young people find botany a dull study. So it is, as taught from the text-books in the schools; but study it yourself in the fields and woods, and you will find it a source of perennial delight. Find your flower, and then name it by the aid of the botany. There is so much in a name. To find out what a thing is called is a great help. It is the beginning of knowledge; it is the first step. When we see a new person who interests us, we wish to know his or her name.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To warn young people that botany is too dull
To urge readers to learn botany through direct observation
To argue that textbooks name flowers inaccurately
To compare learning names of people and plants
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 교과서로 배우는 식물학은 지루하다고 인정하지만 'study it yourself in the fields and woods'라고 권한다. 그렇게 하면 'perennial delight'를 얻는다고 말하며 직접 관찰을 촉구한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 글쓴이의 주장과 반대이고, C는 근거가 없으며 D는 보조 비유에 불과하다.

items.passage: Fines were remitted in spite of all the protests that I could make, several members of the club being allowed to do about as they pleased. There could be but one result, as a matter of course, and that was poor ball playing. When the April campaign ended we were in the eleventh place. At the end of May we stood tenth. At the end of June we had again dropped back to eleventh. At the end of July we had climbed up to eighth, and at the end of August we were sixth, having then climbed into the first division. When the close of the season came, however, we had dropped back again to the ninth position, the margin between sixth and ninth places being a very small one.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To praise the club for its steady climb in rank
To list the fines given to each player that year
To show how lax discipline led to an uneven season
To explain why the narrator resigned from the club
items.explanation: 서술자는 벌금이 면제되고 선수들이 'about as they pleased' 행동했다고 말한다. 그 결과가 'poor ball playing'이라고 밝힌 뒤 순위가 오르내리다 9위로 끝난 시즌을 기록한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 꾸준한 상승(A)은 사실과 다르고 B와 D는 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
We descended to a large dark apartment below the street-level, lighted by a lamp fixed to the wall. Sixty or seventy bodies lay on the floor, some of them quite uncovered, and some wrapped in mats. I could not see distinctly enough by the dim light, to judge of their discoloration. They appeared mostly old and emaciated.

I can not describe the sensation of relief with which I breathed the free air once more. I had no fear of the cholera, but the suffering and misery I had seen, oppressed and half smothered me.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain how cholera spreads in crowded rooms
To praise the workers who cared for the bodies
To argue that the city's officials were negligent
To convey the oppressive effect of a grim scene
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 어두운 지하실에 놓인 'Sixty or seventy bodies'를 묘사한다. 이어 밖으로 나왔을 때의 'relief'를 말하며 본 고통과 비참함이 자신을 'oppressed and half smothered' 했다고 밝힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 콜레라 전파 방식(A), 일꾼 칭찬(B), 관리 비판(C)은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
There had been a strange and unexpected change in the patient's condition, and the doctor had already been there twice. As he put aside his coat and hat and entered her room, it seemed to him that he had forever put aside all else of essay and ambition beyond those four walls. And with the thought a great peace came upon him. It seemed good to him to live for her alone.

It was not for long. As each monotonous day brought the morning mist and evening fog regularly to the little hilltop where his whole being was now centred, she seemed to grow daily weaker, and the little circle of her life narrowed day by day.
items.question: Based on the text, why does the doctor feel a great peace?
options: He has chosen to devote himself wholly to the patient
He believes the patient will soon fully recover
He has finally achieved his professional ambitions
He has been relieved of his duty to the patient
items.explanation: 의사는 방에 들어서며 'all else of essay and ambition'을 내려놓았다고 느낀다. 그 생각과 함께 평화가 찾아왔고 'live for her alone'이 좋다고 여긴다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. 환자는 점점 약해지므로 B는 틀리고, 야망은 버렸으므로 C도 틀리며, D는 지문과 반대다.

items.passage: Ay, and with nothing left of prospect in the future, nor ever any hope. Nothing! nothing! nothing! What had he hoped? he found himself asking: what, in these last few days? What dreamt of? A home, a wife; perhaps, in the future, children waiting for his return, running to meet him and to beg for stories of the sea, of tempests surmounted, of dangers passed. Now, there would never be any home, nor wife, nor children. Nothing! He had loved one woman fondly, madly; the one woman in all the world for him. Until ten minutes ago he had believed that, some day, he would win her. And, now, it was never to be.
items.question: Based on the text, what most causes the man's despair?
options: He has lost his ship in a violent tempest
He learns he cannot win the woman he loves
He fears his children will forget about him
He regrets leaving home to go to sea
items.explanation: 그는 'ten minutes ago'까지 그녀를 언젠가 얻을 수 있다고 믿었다. 그러나 이제 'it was never to be'라고 깨달으며 집과 아내와 아이의 꿈이 사라졌다고 느낀다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 폭풍(A)은 상상 속 이야기 소재이고, 아이들은 아직 없으므로 C는 틀리며, D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
On the way the boy who had been shot through the leg, gave out and had to be carried. The other held up bravely, making frequent and clamorous demands for his gun, and announcing his readiness, severely wounded as he was, to whip the boy who stole it from him. Don kept a still tongue in his head. He had the gun, and being in a better condition to use it than the owner was, he determined to hold fast to it.

When they reached the road they tore a panel or two of the fence to pieces to make a litter for the boy who had given out, and here they were joined by ten or a dozen of their comrades who had left the car by the rear door.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Don keep quiet about the gun?
options: He plans to return it once they reach the road
He is ashamed that he stole it from the boy
He wants to keep a weapon he is fitter to use
He fears the wounded boy will report him
items.explanation: 부상당한 소년은 총을 돌려 달라고 'clamorous demands'를 한다. Don은 'kept a still tongue'했는데, 그가 총을 쓰기에 더 나은 상태였기 때문에 'hold fast to it' 하기로 결심했다고 나온다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 돌려줄 계획(A), 부끄러움(B), 두려움(D)은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: The truth is, that when a guest, of no matter how agreeable a presence, or how attractive an air, has made up his mind to go, the sooner he goes the better. Let him go at once, therefore. Do not press him to stay, or detain him at the door, but “speed” him on his way. It is best for both parties, if they like each other. When, indeed, an unpleasant intruder is about to depart, there is a kind of satisfaction in detaining him a little. We dally with the prospective pleasure of having him gone, till we forget that he is present. But when those we love are leaving us, the best way is, to wink, and part at once; for to be “going” is even worse than to be “gone.”
items.question: Based on the text, why does the writer advise parting quickly from loved ones?
options: Long goodbyes give guests time to reconsider
Hosts secretly wish their guests had stayed away
Quick farewells are more polite to intruders
Lingering over a departure makes it more painful
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 사랑하는 이가 떠날 때 'wink, and part at once'하라고 권한다. 그 이유로 'to be going is even worse than to be gone'이라고 말해 머뭇거림이 고통을 키운다고 본다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 불쾌한 손님은 오히려 붙잡는다고 했으므로 C는 틀리고, A와 B도 근거가 없다.

items.passage: We found ourselves in a large boarding-house, managed by a singularly zealous and kindly master. His care of us was highly amusing during the whole time of our stay. His zeal may be judged of by a circumstance which happened one morning. At breakfast he appeared heated and confused, and looked as if he had a bad headache. He requested us to excuse any forgetfulness that we might observe, and mentioned that he had, by mistake, taken a dangerous dose of laudanum. We begged he would leave the table, and not trouble himself about us, and hoped he had immediately taken measures to relieve himself of the dose. He replied that he had had no time to attend to himself till a few minutes ago.
items.question: Based on the text, why had the master not attended to himself after taking the laudanum?
options: He was too devoted to caring for his guests
He did not believe the dose was dangerous
He wished to hide his mistake from the guests
He was too confused to remember what he took
items.explanation: 서술자는 주인이 'singularly zealous and kindly'했으며 그의 열성을 이 사건으로 알 수 있다고 말한다. 주인은 위험한 약을 먹고도 'no time to attend to himself'였다고 답한다. 따라서 손님 돌보기에 몰두했다는 A가 정답이다. 그는 위험하다고 스스로 밝혔으므로 B와 C는 틀리고, D도 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
On the day of the fire my constitution succumbed to a severe cold, caused by undue exertion in getting ready to do something. I suffered to no purpose, too, because the plan I was figuring at for the extinguishing of the fire was so elaborate that I never got it completed until the middle of the following week.

The first time I began to sneeze, a friend told me to go and bathe my feet in hot water and go to bed. I did so. Shortly afterward, another friend advised me to get up and take a cold shower-bath. I did that also. Within the hour, another friend assured me that it was policy to “feed a cold and starve a fever.” I had both. So I thought it best to fill myself up for the cold, and then keep dark and let the fever starve awhile.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Bitter and resentful
Comically self-mocking
Anxious and fearful
Solemn and reflective
items.explanation: 서술자는 불을 끌 계획이 너무 정교해 다음 주에야 완성됐다며 자신의 쓸모없음을 우스꽝스럽게 말한다. 또 서로 모순되는 친구들의 조언을 모두 따른 뒤 'feed a cold and starve a fever'를 엉뚱하게 해석한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 원망(A), 불안(C), 엄숙함(D)은 이 장난스러운 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Remembering the sweetness of her look and touch on the previous night he had been ready with a smile for her, and her coldness pained him and struck him into silence.

There was a painful pause, as they all heard the sound of the steps of Sir Robert in the hall outside. But when he came in, they were all struck by the change in his manner. Instead of being slow and stately, he was brisk and alert. He did not smile as he bade them all good-morning, and even when he stooped to kiss his son, his face was stern and set.
items.question: Which choice best describes the mood of the text?
options: Cheerful and relaxed
Playful and teasing
Tense and uneasy
Grieving and hopeless
items.explanation: 그는 그녀의 'coldness'에 상처받아 말을 잃고, 이어서 'painful pause'가 흐른다. 들어온 Sir Robert도 웃지 않고 'stern and set'한 얼굴을 보여 긴장을 더한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 명랑함(A)이나 장난스러움(B)은 근거가 없고, 절망적 슬픔(D)은 지나치다.

items.passage:
The isle was barren. Far as hawk may scan
In moors it roll’d up to a headland bare
Save for one narrow patch, by ceaseless care
Sumptuous with corn. Against the sky a Man
Digging the waste I saw,—bow’d veteran
A stubborn spade he drave in stubborn ground
And root and rock flung sheer without a sound
Over the bleak edge.... Then anew began.

“You, who have lodged in the teeth of the abyss
Your cabin low, and triumph rich as this
Wrung from the ocean-bitter mountain side,
What help’d you most to bring such treasure out?”
He stood, and after scrutiny replied,
“The thing on which I lean, the Spade of Doubt.”
items.question: Which choice best describes the tone of the text?
options: Mocking and dismissive
Joyful and carefree
Fearful and despairing
Admiring and contemplative
items.explanation: 화자는 척박한 땅에서 쉬지 않고 일하는 노인을 'bow'd veteran'이라 부르며 그 수확을 'triumph rich as this'라고 칭송한다. 마지막에 노인이 'the Spade of Doubt'라고 답하며 생각할 거리를 남긴다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 조롱(A), 근심 없는 기쁨(B), 절망(C)은 지문의 존경 어린 시선과 맞지 않는다.
